import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Filter out derived features
    non_derived = [i for i, t in enumerate(feats.types) if t != 'derived']
    ids = [feats.ids[i] for i in non_derived]
    
    # Calculate effect sizes (mean difference in outcome groups)
    y = feats.y
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(ids):
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col_idx]
        mean_0 = np.mean(x[y == 0])
        mean_1 = np.mean(x[y == 1])
        effect_size = mean_1 - mean_0
        effect_sizes.append(effect_size)
    
    # Rank by effect size magnitude
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(np.abs(effect_sizes))[::-1]
    
    # Select top drivers
    drivers = []
    seen = set()
    for idx in sorted_indices:
        fid = ids[idx]
        # Skip if highly correlated with already selected drivers
        is_correlated = False
        for d in drivers:
            if abs(stats.pearsonr(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)], 
                                 feats.x[:, feats.column(d)])[0]) > 0.6:
                is_correlated = True
                break
        if not is_correlated:
            drivers.append(fid)
            seen.add(fid)
        if len(drivers) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
            break
    
    # Build columns (only top features)
    columns = []
    for idx in sorted_indices[:10]:  # Limit to top 10 features
        fid = ids[idx]
        columns.append(fid)
    
    # No products to keep model small
    products = []
    
    # Simple weighted score: sum of top drivers with their effect sizes as weights
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(ids):
        if fid in drivers:
            loadings[fid] = effect_sizes[sorted_indices[i]]
    
    return Design(drivers=tuple(drivers), columns=tuple(columns), 
                 products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
